title: Quick check: Server Component Performance

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Server Component Performance”?
options: The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Minimizing unnecessary client JavaScript depends on the selected React framework/runtime and must respect server/client boundaries.
questions.answer_key: Minimizing unnecessary client JavaScript depends on the selected React framework/runtime and must respect server/client boundaries.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Server Component Performance: Minimizing unnecessary client JavaScript depends on the selected React framework/runtime and must respect server/client boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Minimizing unnecessary client JavaScript?
options: Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Confirm the chosen framework supports the API and keep server-only dependencies out of client bundles.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the chosen framework supports the API and keep server-only dependencies out of client bundles.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Server Component Performance: Confirm the chosen framework supports the API and keep server-only dependencies out of client bundles.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Server Component Performance” complete?
options: Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Server Component Performance: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
